description:
FILED s512 (Fable, 2026-10-07) by the static-parsing review (docs/static-parse-limits-review-s512.md, family B).  Probes in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s512/review/static: p02b-tooearly-parens, p02c-tooearly-ref, p11-usesubs, p16-constlater (perl 5.40.3 vs ./pcl on main 3ea47a41).

perl's rule (perlsub, 'Prototypes'): a prototype affects only calls parsed AFTER the sub's declaration or definition is seen; a call parsed before it is a plain list-operator call and perl warns 'main::f() called too early to check prototype'.  A forward declaration `sub f ($);` or `use subs` makes the NAME known at that point (with whatever prototype that spelling carries -- `use subs` carries none).  `use constant NAME` is a `()` sub from its own position.  PCL's `collect_prototypes` (Pl/Parser.pm ~1765, `_walk_prototype_facts`) walks the WHOLE document before any statement is parsed, so every call site sees every prototype.

  no warnings; my @a = (10, 20, 30); print f(@a), "\n"; sub f ($) { $_[0] }          perl 10   PCL 3
  no warnings; my @a = (1, 2, 3); print cnt(@a), "\n"; sub cnt (\@) { ref($_[0]) ? 'ref:'.scalar(@{$_[0]}) : "val:$_[0]" }   perl val:1   PCL ref:3
  use subs qw(sh); my @r = (sh 1, 2); print scalar(@r), "\n"; sub sh ($) { 9 }     perl 1    PCL 2
  print PI * 2, "\n"; use constant PI => 3;                                          perl prints nothing (print to filehandle PI)   PCL 6

WHY IT MATTERS: the common script shape -- main code at the top, prototyped helper subs (`sub trim($)`, `sub max(\@)`) at the bottom, called with parentheses from the top -- runs under perl WITHOUT the prototype and under PCL WITH it; the difference is silent (a count for a list, a reference for a list).  Ordinary programs that live with the 'called too early' warning rely on the un-prototyped behaviour.

FIX SITE: the prototype ENTRY gets the source position of the declaration that introduced it (definition, forward declaration, `use subs` = declared-without-prototype, `use constant`, an import at its `use`, a `:prototype` attribute), and `Pl::Environment::get_prototype` / `_proto_entry` answers only when the asking call site is textually AFTER it -- the parser knows its current position (the walkers are already position-aware for renames, #374(b)); a call site BEFORE the entry gets 'declared, no prototype' when a forward spelling made the name known, else 'unknown'.  Modules' prototypes (the merge, from_module => 1) are at the `use` statement's position.  Guard rows: the four probes above + a `(&@)` block sub called with parens above its definition (perl: the block is an anon sub argument, no difference -- a negative row) + the same calls BELOW the definition (unchanged).  Inverse-verified on the base.  The sweep's sub.t / proto.t rows are the bar.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a PROTOTYPE applies to calls ABOVE its definition -- PCL's prototype table is whole-file, perl's is positional ("called too early to check prototype"): `print f(@a)` with `sub f ($)` BELOW prints 10 in perl (list context, first element), 3 in PCL (count); `(\@)` takes a reference where perl passes the list; `use subs` + a later prototype; `print PI * 2` above `use constant PI`
